Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

after the test i will send mara a screenshot of the preview and the plain text list of items needing review if the result includes any uncertain dates i will ask her to check the envelopes before we change those records and if there are no uncertain dates i will still show her the original status because that was her main concern the test notes need to include the run time the copied file count the review count and any duplicate pairs along with the source names i will leave the 1987 incoming folder in place until she has had a chance to compare the screen with her paper list and then we can decide whether to use another box the next box is labeled winter visitors but we have not opened it yet so it is not part of this run", "output": "We have been maintaining the family photo importer since Aunt Lena asked us to move the scans from her old laptop into the shared archive, and I want to explain what changed during the last two weekends because the next test depends on the folder rules we settled on. The importer reads JPG and JPEG files from an incoming folder and copies them into year and month folders using the date in the image. When that date is missing, it uses the file date but marks the record for review. The original scan stays in the incoming folder until the copy has been checked, and this matters because some of the oldest prints have no reliable date and nobody wants a guessed date to look certain.

On Saturday, I used the small blue USB drive from the hall drawer and copied 214 scans into a test folder on the desktop. The number is the count of source files, not the number of photos, because four files were duplicate scans and one was a text note from Grandpa. The importer skipped the note after checking its extension, but it kept both copies of each duplicate since their filenames were different. The test computer is called Maple and runs Windows 11. The archive share is mounted as Family Archive and has folders through 2023. The newly scanned boxes are from 1987, so we expected the importer to create a 1987 folder and leave later years untouched.

Mara looked at the preview on Sunday and said, “I can tell which pictures need a date, but I cannot tell whether the importer has actually kept the untouched scan.” That is the reason I asked for a visible original status in the preview rather than a second color or another warning symbol. The screen is already busy on her smaller monitor, and she reads it at 125 percent zoom. I tried a green dot first, but she thought it meant the file had been uploaded, so we took the dot out and kept the plain words “original present” beside the filename. The wording is a little dry, but it answers her question without pretending the date is known.

The folder rule needs a careful test because some cameras wrote dates in local time, and some scanners added the day the scan happened instead of the day the photo was taken. The box marked “summer trip” has pictures from two different summers, so its handwritten envelope is useful but not enough to assign every image a year. We agreed that an uncertain date stays uncertain and that the importer should put that item in the review list, not quietly choose the nearest year. When the recorded month is missing, it should still use a known year and put the file in that year folder with “month unknown.” If the year itself is missing, the file stays in incoming until a person can check the envelope.

For the next test, I wrote down the steps in order:
1. Make a fresh copy of the test folder and do not work on the only scan.
2. Open settings and confirm that
archive.retain_originals
is true.
3. Import the 1987 box and note how many files are copied and how many are flagged for review.
4. Open the preview at normal zoom and then at 125 percent to check that “original present” stays readable.
5. Run the same import again and check that it does not make a second copy of files already recorded.

The count should be written in the test notes as copied files, and not as photos, because those are different things.

We found one naming problem during the first run. The scanner had saved a picture as IMG 0041 with a space, and the camera copy was IMG_0041 with an underscore. They appear to show the same kitchen table, but the back of the scan has a pencil mark that is not visible in the camera image, so they are not safe to merge. The importer can compare a checksum to find exact duplicates, but it must not treat similar names as proof that two files are identical. If the checksum matches, it can keep one archive copy and record both source names. If the checksum differs, it should keep both and send them to review. I want the notes to say why a pair was held so we can answer the question later without opening every folder again.

The family has also asked us not to rename the incoming scans before the test because the envelopes have short labels like “cabin” and “school play,” and those labels are sometimes the only clue we have. We can store a cleaned display name in the index, but the source filename needs to remain available next to it. Uncle Peter said, “If I see the name from the scanner, I can match it to my paper list.” I think that is a fair request. The index should show the source name and the suggested folder together, and it should not replace the source name with the date even when the date is clear. We have a separate spreadsheet for the box numbers, and there is no need to add another box number field to this test.

There are two practical limits before the next run. The old laptop disconnects from the share if it sleeps, so I will keep it plugged in and set it not to sleep during the copy. The test folder has about 3 gigabytes free, and the scans total 1.6 gigabytes, so there is room for this run but not for a second full set of originals. The small blue USB drive has 32 gigabytes and is only our backup for the test input, not the archive. The archive share is backed up overnight by the family computer, but I have not checked whether last night’s backup finished, so no one should treat that as confirmation for these new files. We can test the importer without deleting anything and compare the resulting file count with the notes.

After the test, I will send Mara a screenshot of the preview and the plain text list of items needing review. If the result includes any uncertain dates, I will ask her to check the envelopes before we change those records, and if there are no uncertain dates, I will still show her the original status because that was her main concern. The test notes need to include the run time, the copied file count, the review count, and any duplicate pairs along with the source names. I will leave the 1987 incoming folder in place until she has had a chance to compare the screen with her paper list, and then we can decide whether to use another box. The next box is labeled “winter visitors,” but we have not opened it yet, so it is not part of this run."}]
